PMID:15521980.finding: Spanish CLRN1 mutation families show heterogeneous auditory and retinal disease in the Usher syndrome context.
PMID:15521980.read_scope: Complete authentic abstract read; original full article was not recovered. Family-specific vestibular testing and detailed molecular assays remain uninspected.

PMID:15650299.finding: Serial audiometry in 59 Finnish patients and speech testing in 31 document variable progressive hearing impairment.
PMID:15650299.read_scope: Complete authentic abstract read; full original article not recovered. No unavailable individual-patient or Methods detail is asserted.

PMID:19423712.finding: Human 232-residue CLRN1 in HEK293 cells reaches the surface, concentrates in protrusions and changes cortical actin organization; direct actin partners remain unresolved.
PMID:19423712.read_scope: Selected full Methods, Results and Discussion read. The N48K comparison also affects expression and trafficking; mouse knockout bundle findings are a separate species context.

PMID:21310491.finding: P31L and L154W segregate with nonsyndromic retinal disease; the reported localization comparison places wild type at the membrane and mutants in the ER.
PMID:21310491.read_scope: Complete authentic abstract, including its Methods and Results summary, read. Publisher access failed; no full-article assay-to-construct detail is claimed.

PMID:29985171.finding: Mouse deletion and rescue distinguish congenital bundle defects from synaptic actin/calcium-channel disorganization; mouse CLRN1 associates with CaVβ2 and harmonin in tagged assays.
PMID:29985171.read_scope: Selected full Results and Methods plus independently reviewed original supplement establish mouse NP_700434.1 CLRN1 and rat channel constructs. CaVβ2 bridges CLRN1 to the alpha1 interaction domain; endogenous auditory-organ CLRN1 immunodetection failed. This is not direct human binding, purified binary affinity or proof that CLRN1 itself bridges two partners.

PMID:32296183.finding: HuRI records positive binary CLRN1 interactions with diverse proteins, supporting assay-scoped binding annotations.
PMID:32296183.read_scope: Selected full Results and assay/validation legends read; exact target IntAct records, roles, negative flags and constructs inspected separately. The selected cache does not provide a separate Methods section. Native mechanisms or all-product binding are not established by the screen.

PMID:19414487.finding: Mouse Clrn1 deletion produces progressive hearing and vestibular evoked-potential defects, early bundle disorganization and later hair-cell loss.
PMID:19414487.read_scope: Selected actual Methods and Results read, including ABR, DPOAE and VsEP procedures and comparisons. The same model did not show detectable retinal dysfunction at tested ages.

PMID:19539019.finding: Controlled mouse immunolabeling places clarin-1 in developing stereocilia and basal hair-cell regions; UB/OC-1 experiments associate it with microtubules and post-Golgi trafficking.
PMID:19539019.read_scope: Selected Methods, Results and Discussion read, including antibody controls, immunogold, tubulin/nocodazole and tyrphostin/brefeldin comparisons. Historical mouse isoform numbering is not a current human product identifier.

PMID:26180195.finding: Zebrafish loss impairs hearing/balance behavior and mechanically evoked hair-cell responses; native and human-tagged clarin-1 localize to bundles under appropriate fixation.
PMID:26180195.read_scope: Selected Methods and Results read. Human CLRN1-YFP transgenes and native zebrafish protein are distinguished; larval neuromast ribbon numbers were unchanged, which does not negate the separate mouse synaptic findings.

PMID:31625146.finding: Human and animal retinal transcript data favor Müller-glial expression, and biochemical assays detect retinal clarin-1 protein.
PMID:31625146.read_scope: Selected Methods and Results read. Native mouse knock-in retinal immunostaining did not yield a specific signal despite positive Western blotting; transcript localization is not direct subcellular protein imaging.

PMID:40067805.finding: Zebrafish cell-specific rescue supports a Müller-glial contribution to actin-rich apical structures and protection against light-induced photoreceptor loss.
PMID:40067805.read_scope: Selected Results and focused Methods read. Low glial expression rescues whereas high expression can be harmful; rod/cone expression does not provide the same rescue. Altered N-cadherin distribution does not demonstrate a direct CLRN1 adhesion reaction.

PMID:42390169.finding: A CLRN1-null rabbit model develops auditory and late retinal abnormalities, with Müller-glial expression and altered retinal cell profiles.
PMID:42390169.read_scope: Selected Methods, Results and Discussion read. The proposed CLRN1–CTNNA2 protective cascade remains a model; limited Müller-cell counts and a single transcriptomic age constrain causal interpretation. No balance abnormality was detected in the tested conditions.

terms.name: trans-Golgi network transport vesicle
terms.definition: A vesicle that mediates transport between the trans-Golgi network and other parts of the cell.

terms.name: plasma membrane
terms.definition: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

terms.name: protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein.

terms.name: microtubule cytoskeleton
terms.definition: The part of the cytoskeleton (the internal framework of a cell) composed of microtubules and associated proteins.

terms.name: microvillus
terms.definition: Thin cylindrical membrane-covered projections on the surface of an animal cell containing a core bundle of actin filaments. Present in especially large numbers on the absorptive surface of intestinal cells.

terms.name: lamellipodium
terms.definition: A thin sheetlike process extended by the leading edge of a migrating cell or extending cell process; contains a dense meshwork of actin filaments.

terms.name: equilibrioception
terms.definition: The series of events required for an organism to receive an orientational stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Equilibrioception refers to a combination of processes by which an organism can perceive its orientation with respect to gravity. In animals, stimuli come from labyrinth system of the inner ears, monitoring the direction of motion; visual stimuli, with information on orientation and motion; pressure receptors, which tell the organism which body surfaces are in contact with the ground; and proprioceptive cues, which report which parts of the body are in motion.

terms.name: sensory perception of light stimulus
terms.definition: The series of events required for an organism to receive a sensory light stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

terms.name: photoreceptor cell maintenance
terms.definition: Any process preventing the degeneration of the photoreceptor, a specialized cell type that is sensitive to light.

terms.name: basal part of cell
terms.definition: The region of a cell situated near the base. For example, in a polarized epithelial cell, the basal surface rests on the basal lamina that separates the epithelium from other tissue.

terms.name: cell motility
terms.definition: Any process involved in the controlled self-propelled movement of a cell that results in translocation of the cell from one place to another.

terms.name: actin filament organization
terms.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising actin filaments. Includes processes that control the spatial distribution of actin filaments, such as organizing filaments into meshworks, bundles, or other structures, as by cross-linking.

terms.name: positive regulation of lamellipodium assembly
terms.definition: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of the formation of a lamellipodium, a thin sheetlike extension of the surface of a migrating cell.

terms.name: stereocilium
terms.definition: An actin-based protrusion from the apical surface of auditory and vestibular hair cells and of neuromast cells. These protrusions are supported by a bundle of cross-linked actin filaments (an actin cable), oriented such that the plus (barbed) ends are at the tip of the protrusion, capped by a tip complex which bridges to the plasma. Bundles of stereocilia act as mechanosensory organelles.

terms.name: sensory perception of sound
terms.definition: The series of events required for an organism to receive an auditory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Sonic stimuli are detected in the form of vibrations and are processed to form a sound.

terms.name: protease binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protease or a peptidase.

terms.name: protein-macromolecule adaptor activity
terms.definition: An adaptor activity that brings together two or more macromolecules in contact, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. The adaptor can bring together two proteins, or a protein and another macromolecule such as a lipid or a nucleic acid.

terms.name: enzyme binding
terms.definition: Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.

terms.name: structural molecule activity
terms.definition: The action of a molecule that contributes to the structural integrity of a complex.

terms.name: integrin binding
terms.definition: Binding to an integrin.

terms.name: chemokine binding
terms.definition: Binding to a chemokine. Chemokines are a family of small chemotactic cytokines; their name is derived from their ability to induce directed chemotaxis in nearby responsive cells. All chemokines possess a number of conserved cysteine residues involved in intramolecular disulfide bond formation. Some chemokines are considered pro-inflammatory and can be induced during an immune response to recruit cells of the immune system to a site of infection, while others are considered homeostatic and are involved in controlling the migration of cells during normal processes of tissue maintenance or development. Chemokines are found in all vertebrates, some viruses and some bacteria.

terms.name: SNARE binding
terms.definition: Binding to a SNARE (soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attached protein receptor) protein.

terms.name: transmembrane transporter binding
terms.definition: Binding to a transmembrane transporter, a protein or protein complex that enables the transfer of a substance, usually a specific substance or a group of related substances, from one side of a membrane to the other.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–MGST3 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records map the partner to MGST3/O14880. Its authenticated UniProt function and catalytic-reaction entries assign experimentally supported glutathione-transferase/peroxidase activities, establishing enzyme class beyond a domain prediction. GO:0019899 describes binding to that enzyme protein; the screen does not establish CLRN1-dependent catalysis, enzyme regulation or a native shared compartment.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–SEC22B interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify SEC22B/O75396, whose official function and SNARE-complex assignments establish the SNARE protein class. GO:0000149 describes binding to this partner. No CLRN1-mediated vesicle fusion, assembled SNARE-complex binding or particular SNARE-domain contact is inferred from the pair.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–ITGAM interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify ITGAM/P11215, the authenticated integrin alpha-M subunit. GO:0005178 records binding to this integrin protein at the assayed scope. The experiment does not establish contact with an assembled ITGAM/ITGB2 receptor, a native immune-cell interaction or an adhesion mechanism. Different tissue contexts alone do not refute the recorded pair.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–SLC61A1 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify SLC61A1/Q6N075. Its official FUNCTION entry attributes intracellular molybdenum uptake to experimental evidence, providing a functional transporter assignment rather than a name or membrane-domain prediction alone. GO:0044325 describes the bound transmembrane-transporter class. This assessment uses the curated partner record, not a new read of its activity paper, and assigns no transport activity to CLRN1.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–SLC34A3 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify SLC34A3/Q8N130. Its official function and reaction entries establish sodium-dependent phosphate transmembrane transport. GO:0044325 describes binding to that transporter protein; neither CLRN1-mediated flux nor regulation, coupling stoichiometry or a native renal interaction follows from the binding assay.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–TMEM86B interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify TMEM86B/Q8N661. Its official FUNCTION and CATALYTIC ACTIVITY entries attribute lysoplasmalogen hydrolysis to experimental evidence, unlike the domain-only catalytic premise for TMPPE. GO:0019899 is retained for binding to this enzyme protein, without assigning hydrolysis or lipid-metabolic regulation to CLRN1. The partner activity assignment is curated-record evidence, not a newly inspected original activity experiment.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–CCL4L1 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records map the partner to the chemokine protein Q8NHW4/CCL4L1. The official entry establishes chemokine class and separately distinguishes its signal peptide from the mature chain. GO:0019956 describes the mapped partner class at the construct-assay scope. The unsuffixed accession and absent fragment feature do not resolve clone processing, mature-chain contact, exact natural isoform or a native extracellular interaction; those properties are not asserted.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–CANT1 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify CANT1/Q8WVQ1. The official function entry attributes calcium-dependent nucleotidase activity to experiments, supporting enzyme class. GO:0019899 describes this bound protein; the pair does not demonstrate activation or inhibition of CANT1 by CLRN1, secretory-pathway substrate handling or a catalytic function of CLRN1.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–ZDHHC15 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify ZDHHC15/Q96MV8. Its official record attributes protein palmitoylation to experimental evidence, beyond the presence of a DHHC domain. GO:0019899 retains that enzyme-partner specificity without asserting CLRN1 palmitoylation, an enzyme-substrate relationship or modulation of catalytic activity.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–ALG8 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify ALG8/Q9BVK2. Its official glucosyltransferase function and reaction assignments establish enzyme class. GO:0019899 describes the interaction with that protein; the screen does not show that ALG8 glycosylates CLRN1 or that CLRN1 controls oligosaccharide synthesis.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–TMPRSS4 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify TMPRSS4/Q9NRS4. Its official record establishes serine-protease activity and separately annotates proteolytic processing. GO:0002020 identifies the protease protein bound at the tested construct scope; it does not assert that the HuRI construct was activated, that contact involves the mature catalytic chain, or that CLRN1 is cleaved or inhibits the enzyme in vivo.

binding_class_decisions.summary: HuRI records a positive CLRN1–FUT9 interaction.
binding_class_decisions.reason: The three positive HuRI records identify FUT9/Q9Y231. The official function and reaction entries attribute fucosyltransferase activity to experimental evidence. GO:0019899 describes binding to that enzyme protein; a CLRN1 substrate relationship, regulation of fucosylation or a native Golgi mechanism is not established.
